summary: 7-phase plan written from the research's per-assertion dispositions. Phases 1-3 are territory-disjoint (one test file each) and apply dispositions plus cap-burn reduction plus full unmarking; Phase 4 verifies exactly 1 slow-marked test remains repo-wide; Phase 5 deletes the -m "not slow" addopts clause and TEMPORARY comment block; Phase 6 applies task 135's verification bar verbatim (3 separate unfiltered invocations, identical green result set); Phase 7 closes task 135's Phase 7 by reference. Estimated 6 hours.
decisions_made: No budget is re-grounded from p95/p99: research category (a) is empty. Assertions are deleted or converted to behavioural assertions instead, which diverges from the original task description's framing and is stated as such in the plan.

'Narrow to per-test marks on the tests that justify it' resolves to an empty justified set for all three files, so marks are deleted outright rather than pushed down. Exactly one slow-marked test remains repo-wide: models/tests/unit/test_semantic.py::test_max_n_itself_is_constructible.
Both concurrency tests are left byte-identical; re-marking them is superseded and would regress prior work.
Cap-burn reduction (report section 7) is folded into the per-file phases rather than being a separate pass, so each file is edited once.
Phase 5 is a standalone commit so the quarantine deletion can be reverted alone if Phase 6 finds an out-of-scope failure.

Stated scope addition in Phase 5: declare pytest-timeout in pyproject's dev extra. It is installed here but undeclared, and several retained hang guards rely on @pytest.mark.timeout, which would silently become a no-op unknown mark in a clean dev install.
The 3 failures in the research's unfiltered run are all in scope and eliminated by Phases 1-3; Phase 6 requires each to be accounted for by name, not merely absent.
dead_ends: Re-grounding budgets from measured p95/p99 -- the measured distribution's ceiling is the max_time cap, not the code's cost.
Relative scaling ratios between two N values -- measured vacuous under the cap and 3-orders-of-magnitude volatile without it.
Building a benchmark harness inside the functional suite -- trustworthy timing here needs subprocess isolation plus repeat sampling, which is an opt-in benchmarking job.
